items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: That's where I had Clifford Brown and some other very good students.

ctx.x: So, when you worked for a singer, the singer collected the tips and shared them with you, right?
Oh, yes, then they split it up with the band.

Now, how that happened was that a fellow called Freddy Tunstall. Tomsill. He played at the Belmont for Mr. Brown. And he got mad one night, one Sunday night, and left. And Brown knew that I was around there and wasn't working at the time. So he said send somebody and tell them to send for me and I'd come there. He said, "Son, how would you like to go upstairs and play for me?" Cause, he said, "you see, I'm stuck. Freddy's gone back to New York and left me."
